habitat: Small flocks or pairs over grassland. It breeds in river banks and termite mounds, and rests often on a branch or fence.
summary: An uncommon to locally common summer resident. It occurs all year on the northern Botswana and KwaZulu-Natal coastal plains. A large, heavy martin, dark brown above and white below, with a wide brown breast-band, a small white eyebrow, white underwing coverts and a square tail. It twitters while perched or flying. The flight is slow. Months were left unset. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Sand Martin is smaller, with a narrow breast-band, all-dark underwings and no white eyebrow. Banded Martin has the broad band, white eyebrow and square tail.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^1=2 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 1–4.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

underparts.pattern: Wide brown chest-band. White below that.

viewNotes.note: Large and heavy, dark brown above, white below, with a broad brown breast-band and a small white eyebrow.
Broad brown breast-band and white underparts.
White underwing coverts and a square tail. The flight is slow, and it lands often.
White below the broad breast-band, with white underwing coverts.

calls.description: A melodious twitter while perched or flying. Grade A song from the Memel area, Free State. The filename names Banded martin.
